questions.stem: Per this page, which is the KISS way to make a shared counter safe for many threads?

options.text: An `int` field changed with `count++` inside a `synchronized (lock)` block
options.says: The page labels the synchronized block around count++ a violation: custom synchronization for a counter.

options.text: An `int` field changed with `count++` between `lock()` and `unlock()` calls
options.says: The page shows the ReentrantLock counter as the over-engineered approach that violates KISS.

options.text: An `AtomicInteger` field changed with `incrementAndGet()` and no lock at all
options.says: The page says the simplest way is AtomicInteger: lock-free, with no explicit locking needed.

questions.stem: Per this page's decision guide, when should code use a `ReentrantLock` rather than `synchronized`?

options.text: When the code needs tryLock, a timed lock, or Condition objects
options.says: The page's guide: need tryLock, timed lock, interruptible lock or conditions? Use ReentrantLock.

options.text: When the code needs one atomic update of one single variable
options.says: The page's guide sends a single atomic operation on one variable to Atomic*, not to a lock.

options.text: When the code needs plain mutual exclusion around a method
options.says: The page's guide says plain mutual exclusion needs only synchronized.
